transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for the case-management conference in three weeks, I need each of you to share any facts or constraints that should be reflected in our final litigation strategy. Our current draft proposes a broad construction of the principal patent claim, preserves the possibility of injunctive relief, uses ordinary custodial discovery, and permits retention of a technical expert subject to standard internal approval. Please speak up now if there's anything in your area that we need to account for before we finalize the joint report.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a critical issue with our claim-construction strategy. During my review of the patent prosecution file, I found an amendment disclaimer that limits claim 7 to a distributed-cache implementation. This means we cannot pursue the broad construction proposed in the current draft — our litigation position must use the narrow construction 'distributed_cache_only.' I had been checking the file wrapper citations before circulating this note, but given that we need to finalize our strategy before the joint report, I'm disclosing this now so we can revise the claim-construction section accordingly.

My forensic review of the produced data just completed, and it identified responsive technical evidence in exactly four custodians: the platform architect, the former licensee's integration lead, the company's product manager, and the licensee's deployment engineer. The proposed discovery plan should therefore use the exact targeted scope of 'four_named_technical_custodians' rather than the ordinary company-wide custodial discovery currently in the draft. I hadn't updated the draft yet because the forensic review only finished after our last discovery meeting, but we need to revise the discovery section of the joint report accordingly.

In a client steering call this week, the business sponsor told me that preserving the former licensee's distribution relationship is more important than obtaining an immediate market exclusion. The client therefore requires a damages-only litigation posture with no request for injunctive relief, plus a documented business-outreach commitment.
